275.h: Greenfield University is a private university in Kaduna, and the first private university in Kaduna State. Its promoters, led by Engineer Simon Nwakacha, had run nursery, primary and secondary schools in the state for more than 20 years. They told the National Universities Commission of their plan in November 2013, and the university was established in January 2019, beginning its first session that May. The name was chosen to suggest fertile ground for knowledge and skills. In April 2021 the university was the target of a mass kidnapping of students, one of a series of attacks on schools in northern Nigeria at the time.
275.a: The university began with three faculties: Social and Management Sciences, Engineering, and Science and Technology.
275.c: It is located in Kaduna State, in north-western Nigeria.

294.h: Lead City University (LCU) is a private university in Ibadan. It was founded as City University, Ibadan, approved by the National Universities Commission in December 2003 and ratified by the Federal Executive Council on 16 February 2005. The following month its board changed the name to Lead City University, to avoid confusion with similarly named institutions.
294.a: LCU offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes, including medicine and law. Its law programme is accredited by the Council of Legal Education, so its graduates can proceed to the Nigerian Law School. At its 15th convocation, for the class of 2022, it graduated 1,306 undergraduates, 156 of them with first-class degrees, and 534 postgraduates.
294.c: It is located in Ibadan, the capital of Oyo State.

307.h: Novena University was the first private university in Delta State. It was founded in 2005, partly to meet demand from qualified students who could not find places at existing universities, and it is accredited by the National Universities Commission.
307.a: The university has expanded into professional programmes. In 2021 it received approval to start medicine, dentistry and pharmacy, together with health science courses such as nursing, optometry, medical laboratory science, anatomy, physiology and pharmacology. It began an LL.B. law degree in 2022, with a curriculum that includes environmental law, oil, gas and energy law, international trade and cyber security. In June 2024 its nursing degree received full accreditation from the National Universities Commission.
307.c: It is located in Ogume, Delta State.

335.h: The University of Calabar (UNICAL) is a federal university and one of Nigeria's second-generation federal universities. It was a campus of the University of Nigeria until 1975, when it became an independent university. Its motto is 'Knowledge for Service', and its buildings were designed by the architect John Elliott.
335.a: UNICAL offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes in most disciplines, including medicine. Its library, founded in 1975, is one of the largest academic libraries in Nigeria. The university also awards degrees through affiliated institutions approved by the National Universities Commission, including theological seminaries and colleges of education such as the Federal College of Education, Obudu.
335.c: The university is in Calabar, the capital of Cross River State.

339.h: The University of Maiduguri (UNIMAID) is a federal university created in 1975 to become one of the country's principal universities. It is the main university of north-eastern Nigeria. After the death of former President Muhammadu Buhari on 13 July 2025, the Federal Executive Council under President Bola Tinubu approved renaming it Muhammadu Buhari University, Maiduguri.
339.a: The university enrols about 25,000 students. It has a college of medicine and faculties of agriculture, arts, environmental sciences, allied health sciences, basic medical sciences, dentistry, education, engineering, law, management sciences, pharmacy, science, social sciences and veterinary medicine. Its research has grown in agriculture, medicine and conflict resolution, and it runs a university press.
339.c: It is located in Maiduguri, the capital of Borno State.

217.h: Akwa Ibom State University (AKSU) is a public university owned by the Akwa Ibom State Government. On 18 October 2000 Governor Victor Attah inaugurated a committee of academics to plan it as Akwa Ibom State University of Technology. A later administration widened its mission beyond technology and applied science to include the arts, made it a conventional university, and dropped 'of Technology' from its name. It admitted its pioneer students in the 2010/2011 session.
217.a: AKSU runs undergraduate and postgraduate programmes in the sciences, technology, arts and social sciences.
217.c: The university was first planned for a university town within the state's 'technology triangle'. Instead it was set up with its main campus at Ikot Akpaden, in Mkpat Enin local government area. A second campus at Obio Akpa, in Oruk Anam, later became the Federal University of Agriculture and Technology, Obio Akpa.

262.h: Federal University, Birnin Kebbi (FUBK) was established on 18 February 2013, at the same time as the federal universities in Gusau and Gashua, under President Goodluck Jonathan's policy of giving a federal university to each state without one. Its pioneer vice-chancellor was Professor Lawal Suleiman Bilbis, a biochemist and former deputy vice-chancellor of Usmanu Danfodiyo University, Sokoto.
262.a: Teaching began in November 2014 for the 2014/2015 session, with 507 students and 102 academic staff; the first two matriculations, in March 2015 and February 2016, admitted 507 and 972 undergraduates. The university has three faculties and a College of Health Sciences, offering 24 degree programmes, and directorates for academic planning, research and innovation, ICT and entrepreneurship.
262.c: It is located in Birnin Kebbi, the capital of Kebbi State in north-western Nigeria.

342.h: The University of Port Harcourt (UNIPORT) is a public research university. It was established in 1975 as University College, Port Harcourt, and gained full university status in 1977. In 2015 Times Higher Education ranked it first in Nigeria and sixth in Africa.
342.a: UNIPORT began in 1977 with schools of humanities, social sciences, biological, chemical and physical sciences, educational studies and science laboratory technology, and changed to a faculty system in 1982. It now has fourteen faculties, among them Engineering, Management Sciences, Science, Computing, Agriculture, Law, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Dentistry and a College of Health Sciences, as well as a Faculty of Communication and Media Studies accredited in 2023. Its engineering and geosciences programmes are closely linked to the oil and gas industry of the Niger Delta.
342.c: The campus lies at Aluu and Choba, on the outskirts of Port Harcourt, Rivers State.
